lines.say: Do you need to eat more to build muscle?
So most people grow best when they eat a little more than they burn. That's a surplus.
But a bigger surplus doesn't build more muscle. It mostly adds fat.
In one study of athletes, the bigger surplus group gained more fat, without clearly more muscle.
A good target: gain about a quarter to half a percent of your body weight a week.
For an eighty kilo person, that's about two to four hundred grams a week.
Beginners and people with extra fat can often build muscle without a surplus.
